environment_limitation.summary: Live WebGL rendering could not be observed this session for any of the three pilots, so per-pilot draw calls, triangles, geometry/texture counts, FPS samples and real screenshots are not available.
diagnostic_evidence: computer{action:'screenshot'} failed with 'the Browser pane is not displayed, so the page is not compositing frames' on every attempt, including after resize_window and after a real ref-based click that gained document.hasFocus()=true
a direct requestAnimationFrame counter probe recorded 0 callbacks over 57.7 real seconds in the same tab, confirming the render loop itself never ran (not merely a screenshot-tool issue)
consequently canvas.width/height stayed at the browser's un-set default (300x150) and window.__drift3dEvidence-equivalent snapshot reported canvasPresent:false throughout

Claude in Chrome (the real-Chrome fallback that obtained genuine measurements for this same class of problem during DRIFT-IV-SYS-70/DRIFT-IV-BY-EUX-20/30) reported 'extension isn't reachable' on two separate connection attempts this session
the user was asked how to proceed (open the Browser pane / connect Claude in Chrome / proceed with honest limitation) and explicitly chose to proceed with honest limitation documentation
environment_limitation.not_a_code_defect: This is the same class of sandboxed-automation-browser compositor block this project has documented multiple times before (DRIFT-IV-SYS-70, DRIFT-IV-BY-EUX-20, DRIFT-IV-BY-EUX-30) — a background/non-composited tab throttles requestAnimationFrame and (by extension) ResizeObserver-driven Canvas sizing to zero, independent of any application code. It is not evidence of a pilot defect.

resource_disposal_across_switches.note: Disposal code exists and runs on React unmount for all three pilots (geometry/material/texture .dispose(), mixer.uncacheRoot, InstancedMesh removal), and React's own unmount guarantee (a different component type mounted in the same conditional slot triggers full unmount of the previous one, not an update) means this fires on every pilot switch by construction — but the actual GPU-resource-count-stays-bounded claim could not be confirmed live this session (gl.info.memory.geometries/textures via the dev-only Drift3DKitPilotMemoryProbe never produced a non-zero reading, consistent with the render loop never starting). One exception is architectural, not session-specific: Water.js's internal reflection WebGLRenderTarget has no public accessor, so it cannot be explicitly .dispose()d by this pilot regardless of environment — documented as a known upstream three.js addon limitation.

owner_live_review_resolution.note: This section resolves the functional/acceptance question this file's environment_limitation and per_pilot_render_metrics sections above could not answer this session — it does not retroactively convert any null numeric field to a measured value. The owner personally ran all three pilots in Drift Kit Lab, on their own local machine, in a session this agent did not observe, and confirmed: 'Everything is OK in Drift Kit Lab, although it is severely lacking in realistic graphics.' This is first-hand confirmation that the pilots load, run, and are usable end-to-end (resolving the functional-viability question), combined with an explicit artistic reservation on visual realism (see shared-kit-pilots-evidence.md/.json §12 / owner_live_review for the full record). It does not supply any FPS/draw-call/triangle/geometry/texture number — every such field in per_pilot_render_metrics above remains null and KNOWN_ENVIRONMENT_LIMITATION, honestly, because no such number was measured or reported.
